doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Milt Hinton on his first album as leader
summary: Arbors' Mat Domber let him choose everything; he hired Milt Hinton, who set everyone at ease and knew when to push on.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You’ve got two, at least two, under your own name now?
One almost brand new? And on your first album you had Milt Hinton?
That must have been a good experience.

Oh, boy, yeah. Well he was the highlight of that session for me, which was full of great musical moments and playing with great guys. Again, they were all top-notch guys. Mat Domber of Arbors Records was great because he asked me to do this CD after having done a few as a sideman for him. And of course that was a great thrill and honor. But also he really left it in my hands to pick the guys and the tunes and the studio and the engineer, and so I really got to do it my own way and write some original tunes and arrangements. And as I was considering who to hire for this record, I started thinking of guys and of course you want to play with guys that you feel comfortable with and guys that are the best guys available and guys that you think will sound good together, and I was thinking about a bass player and I thought well why not just start at the top? You know and the worst thing he can say is no, right? So I went who’s the best bass player I’ve played with, and I had done maybe a half dozen gigs with Milt Hinton. I thought well you can’t really beat him. And so I called him up and he was really nice about it. You know because I think like the pay was probably less than he’s used to because he’d been used to playing on bigger labels and stuff like that. So I think he made an exception

because he’s always liked to help out and encourage younger players who he felt were on the right track or trying to keep the music going and all of that. So he did it and I was thrilled. And he was a great help and a great inspiration in the studio. There was times when I would start to count off a tune and I’d think wait a second, I should ask Milt to count this tune off. Because he was on like the original recording of it and has played it with all the best bands in history. And if anybody knows what tempo this should be it’s going to be him. And so that was a nice thing to be able to sort of fall back on him and use his experience and try to just take advantage of him in the best way possible as far as just using his inspiration. And he had such a good feeling of warmth about him in the studio. He kept everybody at ease. You’d think playing with him would have you terrified or something, but he has a way of putting you at ease and just making things feel comfortable. And he’d tell some little stories when he’d have a little break, and some of that Mat captured on video, too. That should be in some archive too, I guess it’s in Mat’s archives. But that’s pretty neat. I’ve got a copy of that. And the other thing that’s funny, you know he was the oldest guy in the band by far. I don’t recall, he might have been 80 at the time, or 79 or something like that. But he also seemed to have the most energy. It’s amazing. You know he was in great shape and playing at the top of his form. And there was times when I was very concerned about making sure he was comfortable and that we weren’t overworking him. And so there was times when I’d just kind of look around and act like I was talking with the whole band when really I was thinking of him. I’d say, “Well maybe it’s time we should take a break now,” you know I didn’t want anybody to feel overworked. But he knew when we should keep going, like say the band was starting to get a groove going, and a nice energy, and there’s times like that where people like him know that, let’s knock another song out right away because he knew that we all had this groove going and we could do that. And he was always right. Because usually when he’d say that we’d knock some song off in one take because everybody just had this momentum going. So he was great that way.
That’s terrific. He’s a real treasure.
Oh, I’ll say. Yeah. I was very thrilled to have him there.
